gaps.sentence: She was praised for her ___ (TOLERATE) of other viewpoints.
The medicine is available without a ___ (PRESCRIBE).
There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: Do you believe in the ___ (EXIST) of life on other planets?
gaps.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: existence (-ence noun).

gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: The referee sent him off for repeated ___ (OBEY).
gaps.explanation: 'Repeated disobedience' — the negative noun follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.
